(Fort Smith, Arkansas) | college = [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]] (2020–2022) | highlights = * First-team All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] – Coaches (2022) * Second-team All-SEC – [[Associated Press|AP]] (2022) * SEC All-Defensive Team (2022) }} '''Jaylin Williams''' (born June 29, 2002) is an American professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas Razorbacks]]. ==High school career== Williams played basketball for [[Northside High School (Fort Smith, Arkansas)|Northside High School]] in [[Fort Smith, Arkansas]], where he was teammates with [[Isaiah Joe]].{{cite web |last1=Allen |first1=Nate |title=Fort Smith Northside duo contribute big at Arkansas |url=https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2021/nov/27/fort-smith-northside-duo-contribute-big-at/ |website=[[Arkansas Democrat-Gazette]] |access-date=June 13, 2022 |date=November 27, 2021}} As a sophomore, he helped his team reach the Class 7A state final.{{cite web |last1=Dawson |first1=Dudley E. |title=Fort Smith Northside's Williams continues sprouting up |url=https://www.wholehogsports.com/news/2018/apr/07/fort-smith-northsides-williams-continues-sprouting/?f=recruiting |publisher=WholeHogSports |access-date=June 13, 2022 |date=April 7, 2018}} In his junior season, Williams averaged 16 points, 11 rebounds and three blocks per game,{{cite web |title=Jaylin Williams |url=https://arkansasrazorbacks.com/roster/jaylin-williams/ |publisher=Arkansas Razorbacks |access-date=June 13, 2022}} and was named Arkansas Division I Player of the Year by the ''Northwest Arkansas Democrat-Gazette''.{{cite web |title=DI Boys Player of the Year: Jaylin Williams • FS Northside |url=https://www.nwaonline.com/news/2019/apr/07/di-boys-player-year-jaylin-williams-fs-northside/ |website=[[The Northwest Arkansas Times]] |access-date=June 13, 2022 |date=April 7, 2019}} He led his team to the Class 6A state title and was named tournament MVP after recording 20 points and 16 rebounds in the title game.{{cite web |last1=Taylor |first1=Erick |title='Humble' Northside earns respect |url=https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2019/mar/09/humble-northside-earns-respect-20190309/ |website=[[Arkansas Democrat-Gazette]] |access-date=June 13, 2022 |date=March 9, 2019}} As a senior, Williams averaged 18.7 points, 12.2 rebounds, 2.7 assists and 2.5 blocks per game, earning Arkansas [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]] honors and repeating as Arkansas Division I Player of the Year.{{cite web |title=Williams named Gatorade Arkansas Player of the Year |url=https://www.swtimes.com/story/sports/high-school/basketball/2020/03/27/williams-named-gatorade-arkansas-player/1451816007/ |website=[[Southwest Times Record]] |access-date=June 13, 2022 |date=March 27, 2020}}{{cite web |last1=Boyd |first1=Paul |title=All-NWADG Basketball: Williams expands game looking to college |url=https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2020/mar/27/all-nwadg-division-i-boys-basketball-wi/ |website=[[Arkansas Democrat-Gazette]] |access-date=June 13, 2022 |date=March 27, 2020}} A consensus four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], he committed to playing college basketball for [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]] over an offer from [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]], among other programs.{{cite web |last1=Davenport |first1=Richard |title=Fort Smith Northside's Jaylin Williams commits to Arkansas |url=https://www.nwaonline.com/news/2019/nov/23/big-man-jaylin-williams-commits-arkansas/ |website=[[The Northwest Arkansas Times]] |access-date=June 13, 2022 |date=November 23, 2019}} ==College career== As a freshman at Arkansas, Williams averaged 3.7 points and 4.7 rebounds per game.{{cite web |last1=Jones |first1=Taylor |title=Jaylin Williams Deserves More Respect |url=https://razorbackswire.usatoday.com/2022/03/02/jaylin-williams-deserves-more-respect/ |publisher=Razorbacks Wire |access-date=June 13, 2022 |date=March 2, 2022}} He became a regular starter in his sophomore season.{{cite web |last1=Collier |first1=Jackson |title=2021-22 Season in Review: Jaylin Williams |url=https://arkansas.rivals.com/news/2021-22-season-in-review-jaylin-williams |publisher=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] |access-date=June 13, 2022 |date=May 21, 2022}} Williams averaged 10.9 points and 9.8 rebounds per game, receiving first-team All-[[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) honors from the league's coaches. He was a second-team All-SEC selection by the [[Associated Press]] and made the All-Defensive Team. Williams led the [[NCAA Division I]] with 54 [[charge (basketball)|charges]] drawn and grabbed 364 rebounds, setting a program single-season record. He entered the [[2022 NBA draft]] and opted to forgo his remaining college eligibility.{{cite web |last1=Whaley |first1=Logan |title=Jaylin Williams staying in NBA Draft, will not return to Arkansas |url=https://www.ky3.com/2022/05/30/jaylin-williams-staying-nba-draft-will-not-return-arkansas/ |publisher=KY3 |access-date=June 13, 2022 |date=May 30, 2022}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://arkansasrazorbacks.com/roster/jaylin-williams/ Arkansas Razorbacks bio] [[Category:2002 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Arkansas]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Fort Smith, Arkansas]] [[Category:Power forwards (basketball)]] [[Category:Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball players]]
